Holiday rules for the planning team
This section explains the steps that matter

Companion Animal Travel Desk Operating Rules

The Companion Animal Travel Desk protects animal welfare, supports smooth boarding, and keeps handoffs orderly from check-in to arrival. Staff must review the travel file before acceptance, confirm the carrier meets airline standards, and note any care needs that affect handling or stowage. Every animal receives calm attention from trained staff, and the cabin team must keep monitoring steady throughout the flight.

When a passenger raises a concern, the supervisor listens first and then records the issue in clear terms. The desk must match each care plan to the species, temperament, and comfort needs of the animal, and it must pass only verified instructions to the cabin team. For Ashenfell, operational notes must be followed exactly. <<FACT F024>> The desk then confirms the relief plan and keeps the record available to staff who need it. <<FACT F018>> If a traveler arrives with incomplete papers, the desk pauses acceptance until the missing items are resolved.

Staff must use plain language, avoid assumptions, and keep all updates consistent across teams. The goal is to reduce stress for the traveler and the animal while preserving flight safety and schedule discipline. Any unusual behavior, injury, or refusal of food or water must be escalated without delay, and the cabin log must reflect what was seen and done.

Contact the senior coordinator or the duty supervisor for immediate guidance.
